why: Programs the interpreter in the tab may be able to run before the
compiler this site advertises can. scripts/check-ahead.mjs runs each one
through the module the build publishes and, for every one that RUNS,
requires the named anchor to be present in the pinned compiler's
spec/anchors.json. A witness that runs here and names a clause the
release does not declare reddens the build (wolf-web#35).
A witness the module refuses is not a failure: it means the tab is not
ahead on that clause, which is the ordinary state. The entry stays so
that the day the interpreter mirrors it early, the gate is already
`stdout` is asserted whenever the program runs, because 'it runs' is only
a claim about the clause if it answers the way the clause says it should.

witnesses.name: a one-line if
note: The first case, and the one this gate was written from. lupin 0.1.33
ran it while wolf v0.2.10 refused it: the clause text was read from
wolf-lang trunk f608487, which landed after the v0.2.10 tag, and the
interpreter's own release notes said so. The counted pin lag was
ZERO at that pin and the pages said `the same commit`, which was
correct arithmetic about revisions and an incomplete claim about
behaviour — a reader could copy this out of the playground and watch
their compiler refuse it. It closed at v0.2.11, so it is green now;
the planted case in tests/ahead-witnesses.test.mjs is what proves
witnesses.program:
fn main() -> !int {
    let n = 29
    let m = if n > 10 then n - 1 else n + 1
    print("{n}")
    print("{m}")
    0
}
